newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha quiet, eyes on crude direction.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha quiet, eyes on crude direction.

text.p: The Tokyo naphtha market was deserted in late afternoon trade on Tuesday, with sellers sidelined following news that the U.S. military launched cruise missile strikes against Iraq, traders said.
"Sellers backed right off the market to see how overseas crude markets react to the U.S. action," one trader said.

Open-spec naphtha for first-half November was notionally assessed at $205.00/$208.00, compared with Tuesday morning's $200.00/$201.00 quotes. Sellers would come back to the market only after they have examined the direction of crude in the London market, traders said.
Petrochemical end-users said they were concerned about the stability of naphtha supplies as well as price hikes.
Japan satisfies about 60 percent of its domestic naphtha demand with imports, and has term contracts with Middle Eastern oil producers such as Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Abu Dhabi.
In spreads, first-half November/first-half December was nominally quoted at even/plus $1.50, and second-half November/second-half December at plus $1.00/$1.50.
Players in the middle distillates market were also on the sidelines, awaiting the London opening, traders said.
